fields.name: sustain
fields.description: Attack = ramp up, Decay = drop to sustain level, Sustain = plateau, release = ramp off. Image search for ADSR envelopse online for a visual representation of the curve. Sustain is the plateau of camera shake (time in seconds).

fields.name: sustain_multiplier
fields.description: The sustain multiplier is a proportion of the maximum attack value on the curve.   So, if the maximum attack value reaches 2.5 and the sustain multiplier is 0.5, then the sustain value is 1.25.  Image search for ADSR envelope online for a visual representation of the attack,decay,sustain,release curve.

fields.description: When factions are added to a quest battle, the game will try to deploy only the strongest army from a faction regardless of attached deployment zones. Therefore it is recommended to use as many different qb factions as possible for the same race, to avoid such side effect.  Bare in mind that they need to have a start_pos_factions entry to be eligible.  The bare minimum should be 1 different faction for each army deployed

fields.name: change_max_angle
fields.description: Determines the maximum angle for the random change in direction of travel. Max is 360 degrees. 0 means that angle will never be changed.

fields.name: contact_effect
fields.description: If the vortex hits an entity, this ‘special_ability_phase’ will be applied on their unit.

fields.name: damage
fields.description: base damage dealt by the vortex at 100% damage scaling. Damage scales linearly towards the edge of the vortex radius.

fields.name: damage_ap
fields.description: armour-piercing damage dealt by the vortex at 100% damage scaling.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Determines how long a vortex explosion will last in seconds.

fields.name: expansion_speed
fields.description: Determines the rate of expansion for the vortex. This value is per second. Expansion speed is also multiplied with ‘detonation_force’ to calculate momentum for impacts (knock back, knocked down, knocked flying). Note, vortices can have negative expansion speed, which will drag entities towards the centre of the vortex. If you use a negative expansion speed, start and goal radius need to be the same.

fields.name: goal_radius
fields.description: Determines the ultimate radius for the vortex. The vortex explosion will expand per second according to the ‘expansion_speed’ until goal radius is reached.

fields.name: infinite_height
fields.description: if set to yes the vortex will become a cylinder with infinite height rather than a globe.

fields.name: move_change_freq
fields.description: Determines how frequently the vortex movement will change direction of travel. This represents seconds.

fields.name: movement_speed
fields.description: Determines whether the centre of the vortex will move and a what speed. If movement_speed is 0, the vortex will stay static. This speed is meters per second.

fields.name: start_radius
fields.description: Determines the starting radius for the vortex. This is in meters.

fields.name: ignition_amount
fields.description: If set to a value higher than 0, it will deal fire damage.

fields.name: is_magical
fields.description: if yes it will deal magical damage.

fields.name: composite_scene
fields.description: links to a ‘composite_scene’, which is how we deliver the VFX and sounds for vortices.

fields.name: detonation_force
fields.description: Determines the force of impact for the vortex explosion. Multiplied with expansion speed to determine impact momentum.

fields.name: launch_source
fields.description: determines where the vortex will be launched from. Target_centre is used for explosions and vortices, target_near_centre for winds and breaths, activator front for vortices like night goblin fanatics.

fields.name: building_collision
fields.description: If the vortex centre collides with a building, will it “1.ignore”= bounce back into the opposite direction of travel or “2. Expire”=end.

fields.name: height_off_ground
fields.description: Determines the height for the centre of the vortex. Keep this at 0 unless you want to make a vortex that hits flyers mostly.

fields.name: delay
fields.description: We do spawn this at the same time as usual, but we wait this time to cause damage / move / collide etc.

fields.name: num_vortexes
fields.description: How many vortices do we spawn. These are staggered, launching one per second.

fields.description: Blood version

fields.name: affects_allies
fields.description: Does it affect friendly units

fields.name: launch_source_offset
fields.description: used by AI to optimal targeting offset for breaths and winds.

fields.description: Via group we can configure multiple composite scenes per Vortex Spell

fields.name: army_funding_cap
fields.description: In case of inactivity (left number of turns not spending), the size of this budget pool will be restricted to the specified amount. So you can setup things like: if the construction budget isn't used for 5 rounds, only allow 1000 money to be stored here, distribute the rest among other pools.

fields.description: If this pool isn't being used at all for the specified amount of rounds, the AI will "release" this pool and will only put a restricted amount here (x_funding_cap), the rest will be distributed among other pools. As soon as the pool gets used, this timer re-sets and the AI changes back to the normal usage of the pool. This is to ensure that the AI doesn't hold money in unused pools

fields.description: Has very little effect in game, the only impact it has is to reduce the link between attitude and AI strategic stance (whether the AI is friendly, very friendly, unfriendly... ) towards another faction. With higher aggressiveness factions generally having a lower strategic stance than thier attitude would suggest

fields.name: technology_manager_key
fields.description: The technology stystem works by selecting a path via weighted random distribution according to the given priorities, technologies within this path are then researched by weighted random selection according to given priorities. Once a path is chosen the AI will complete that path unless it is unable to select any further technologies within that path. If there are no valid paths available (or left) the AI will randomly select from all available technologies. Therefore, I recommend only putting the best techs within each path structure into this system as this will ensure the AI always focuses on them, only researching the less good ones when new paths aren't available

fields.name: parent
fields.description: Fallback parent of this group, forming a tree. The military generator walks UP this chain: a unit matches the closest ancestor group its template defines a ratio for, and if a template's group has no recruitable units, its ratio is passed to the parent (repeatedly, until a populated group is found). Fallback only triggers when the faction can recruit ZERO unit types in the group — caps/cost do not trigger it. An explicit ratio of 0 on a group in a template blocks fallback through it. Chains must be loop-free, and a unit must not be tagged into two groups sharing the same root (validated at load).

fields.name: tier
fields.description:
Used in the UI to show the Tier of unit

This is the general rule for approximating a unit tiers:
=IF([@[multiplayer_cost]]=0, - do nothing
IF([@[multiplayer_cost]] is less than 500, - unit tier 1,
IF([@[multiplayer_cost]] is less than 1000, - unit tier 2,
IF([@[multiplayer_cost]] is less than 1500, - unit tier 3,
IF([@[multiplayer_cost]] is less than 2000, - unit tier 4,
else - unit tier 5

fields.description: This is the maximum angle that the projectile can be fired at. Generally you want it high (max 90 degrees), and above 45. Except for special cases (e.g. cannon). Not used when trajectory is fixed!

fields.description: This describes the speed the projectile launches at (metres per second). If it is negative, the code will calculate this value based on firing at 45 degrees, hitting at the effective range. Not used when trajectory is fixed!

fields.name: marksmanship_bonus
fields.description: Bonus to accuracy inherent to projectile. Reduces size of calibration area together with a land_units accuracy stat.

fields.name: collision_radius
fields.description: Used to calculate whether a projectile collides with a building.

fields.name: calibration_distance
fields.description: The distance at which the calibration area is at 100%.

fields.name: calibration_area
fields.description: The area within which the projectile can land when fired. Scales according to calibration distance and is reduced further by accuracy and marksmanship bonus.

fields.name: bonus_v_infantry
fields.description: deals extra damage to entities that are small or very small. This bonus damage used the armour-piercing ration of the total projectile damage.

fields.name: bonus_v_large
fields.description: deals extra damage to entities that are medium or larger. This bonus damage used the armour-piercing ration of the total projectile damage.

fields.name: overhead_stat_effect
fields.description: Apply this special ability phase when projectile travels over a unit.

fields.name: shockwave_radius
fields.description: Determines radius around the projectile where damage will still be dealt. Allows near misses to still deal damage.

fields.name: contact_stat_effect
fields.description: Apply this special ability phase when projectile hits a unit.

fields.name: gravity
fields.description: Use this value to make projectiles be more / less affected by gravity. This is mainly used as a representation of wind resistance, so that projectiels can hang in the air. Negative means to use 'normal' gravity.

fields.name: scale
fields.description:
A multiplier that dictates the visual scale of an entity. i.e. Setting this to 2 will make your unit 200% bigger than the scale that the asset has been authored at.

If this variant is a rider of a War Beast macro entity, this multiplier will not have any effect. A rider's scale is set by the mount.

Note: This does not matter for Chariots, which use the rider scale independantly of the mount scale.

If this variant is a mount of a War Beast macro entity, set it to the scale that you wish the rider to be. Then adjust the value in the mount_scale column in order to multiply up to the value you want. i.e. If an Arachnarok Spider is scale 4, but has a character rider that is scale 1.15, set the scale to be 1.15, then the mount_scale to be 3.48 (in order to multiply back up to 4).

Sync Rider Cavalry variants must be configured to use an agreed-upon scale before animation begins, in order to avoid de-sycnchronisation.

key.lookup_hardcoded: assume_failure_score;;;;;(real) If an item's score while performing analysis is ever less than this value, we skip performing later queries. This acts as an optimization so that queries intended as strict filters can be run first, leaving more detailed analysis and queries to only be performed if they fail. The default value is -9.9 so that a negative score of -10 ensures failure (epsilon of 0.1 for potential float inaccuracy).:::::normalize_scores;;;;;(boolean) Whether we should normalize scores before selection. This occurs after score_threshold_min, but before treat_score_as_probability has taken place. If there is no scoring, or all scores are otherwise 0, then all scores will be set to 1.:::::number_of_items_to_select;;;;;(cardinal) How many different items in the policy the algorithm will attempt to select:::::score_combine_method;;;;;("additive", "multiplicative") How query scores are combined:::::score_threshold_min;;;;;(real) The minimum score that an item must have to be considered for selection:::::treat_score_as_probability;;;;;(boolean) After selection, whether to treat scores as a probability. If this value is true, potentially filter out selected items by running a random roll between 0-1 and checking if the item's score is lower than this number.

pick_all;;;;;Chooses everything. This is equivalent to "pick_best" with number_of_decision_items_to_select being infinity.:::::pick_best;;;;;Chooses by picking the highest-scored items.:::::weighted_random_select;;;;;Chooses by treating each item's score as a weight, to do a weighted random select between. Note that negative or zero scores are invalid in this case: score_threshold_min should be at least 0.

allied_foreign_slots;;;;;Supports the allied buildings mechanic. This handles opening of slots in regions, but the actual construction of buildings in these slots is handled normally through the cai construction system. Expects a non-record-bound decision type. Should be targeted at a region.:::::caravans;;;;;Supports caravans / ivory road for Cathay. Initially we planned to support selection of routes, but as the GDS does not have "caravan routes" as a domain concept this instead just is used to determine when to create a caravan, but not where. A random family member will be chosen to create a caravan, which will then randomly choose a start node and end node to path between. Expects a non-record-bound decision type. Does not require a target.:::::character_initiatives;;;;;Used for character initiatives. Expects an initiative set and an initiative if the clear flag is not set. Optional clear flag removes either every initiative within the set if no initiative is specified, or a specific initiative.:::::compass;;;;;Cathay / winds-of-magic compass support. This feature is fairly simple, just choosing 1 of 4 "directions" for the faction. Expects a compass_directions record. Optionally takes a compass_actions record. Does not require a target.:::::devotees;;;;;Devotees support for Slaanesh, and potentially slaves support for Dark Elves. Picked per-faction-province. Similar to provincial initiatives, but selection of >1 item simultaneously is valid. Expects a non-record-bound decision type. Should be targeted as a faction_province.:::::diplomacy_manipulation;;;;;Diplomacy manipulation. One half of Tzeentch changing-of-the-ways mechanics, for the diplomatic operations. Other half of changing-of-the-ways is implemented via rituals decision system. Expects a non-record-bound decision type. Requires a third_party as a faction, and target as either faction or region.:::::disband_military_forces;;;;;Used to disband military forces. This was implemented for gds-driven undeploying of ogre camps, but can be used to disband any military force if desired. Expects a non-record-bound decision type. Should be targeted at a resource_mobile (as a military force).:::::faction_initiatives;;;;;Used for faction initiatives, i.e. Chaos Gifts. Expects both an initiative set and an initiative. Adding the optional clear flag makes it clear the specified initiative from the current faction if it exists.:::::manipulate_winds_of_magic;;;;;Used for Tzeentch Grimoires, increasing/decreasing WoM levels in a province. Expects a non-record-bound decision type. Should be targeted at a province.:::::military_force_plagues;;;;;Was originally used for Nurgle plagues, before design changed. Now used as an unlockable feature for Daemon Princes. Used for picking a plague per-army. Expects a plagues record. Should be targeted at a resource_mobile (as a military force).:::::occupation_decision;;;;;Supporting settlement occupation decisions. Expects either an settlement_occupation_decisions record or a culture_settlement_occupation_options record. If using a settlement_occupation_decisions record, it will choose a random culture-specific option, while if it uses a culture_settlement_occupation_options record it'll choose that precise culture-specific option. Must be used with activation point "z_occupation_decision".:::::promise_of_perfection;;;;;Used for Slaanesh promise of perfection / unit bribery. Expects a non-record-bound decision type. Must only be used with activation point "z_prebattle_unit_bribery".:::::province_initiatives;;;;;Used for provincial initiatives, i.e selecting a per-faction-province buff. Similar to devotees. Expects either a provincial_initiatives record or a non-record-bound decision type. Should be targeted at a faction_province.:::::region_initiatives;;;;;Used for region initiatives. Expects initiative and initiative set.:::::rift_realm;;;;;Supports rift teleportation to a realm. Expects a teleportation_node_template. Technically this system isn't necessary, as rift_releport can be used with a teleportation_node_template, but this only became obvious to me after I'd already implemented the interface...:::::rift_teleport;;;;;Supports rift teleportation to any node. Expects a non-record-bound type. Filters the available nodes by the teleportation_node_template (which may be null, which represents non-realm nodes).:::::rituals;;;;;Rituals support. This is used to drive numerous gameplay systems, and is used by almost all factions in one way or another. Expects a rituals record, and optionally a cai_plague_recipes record. Depending on the ritual type, can be targeted at a faction, region or resource_mobile (as a military force).:::::stub;;;;;Is used to support GDS-driven analyzers and debugging. This system does nothing. Selection of an item using system may be utilized whenever you don't want an action to occur, for example as an explicit "do_nothing" item if you want to score "yes/no" options separately instead of utilizing algorithm minimum scores. Expects nothing. Does not require a target.:::::summon_spawnable_force_at_force;;;;;Supports conditionally spawnable forces, such as ogre camps and Slaanesh summon disciple armies mechanics. Expects a conditionally_spawnable_forces record. Should be targeted at a resource_mobile (as a military force).:::::trespass_warning;;;;;Supports "get-off-my-land", i.e trespass warnings. Expects a non-record-bound decision type. Should be targeted at a faction.

allied_foreign_slots_open_slots;;;;;allied_foreign_slots: Attempts to open a foreign slot in the targeted region.:::::caravans_create_new;;;;;caravans: Attempts to create a new ivory road caravan using a random family member as it's leader. This caravan will automatically choose a start node, end node, and path. The amount of cargo taken is determined by personality variables caravans_minimum_cargo, caravans_maximum_cargo, caravans_maximum_cargo_as_proportion_of_treasury and caravans_cargo_increments.:::::character_initiatives_clear;;;;;character_initiatives: Clears all selected Character Initiatives for the targeted character.:::::devotees_clear;;;;;devotees: Clears all devotees options in the targeted faction_province.:::::devotees_growth;;;;;devotees: Selects the "growth" devotees/slave effect buff in the targeted faction_province.:::::devotees_income;;;;;devotees: Selects the "income" devotees/slave effect buff in the targeted faction_province.:::::devotees_public_order;;;;;devotees: Selects the "public_order" devotees/slave effect buff in the targeted faction_province.:::::diplomacy_manipulation_break_alliance;;;;;diplomacy_manipulation: Attempts to utilize diplomacy manipulation to break an alliance between the target faction and third_party faction.:::::diplomacy_manipulation_force_war;;;;;diplomacy_manipulation: Attempts to utilize diplomacy manipulation to force a war between the target faction and third_party faction.:::::diplomacy_manipulation_transfer_settlement;;;;;diplomacy_manipulation: Attempts to utilize diplomacy manipulation to transfer the target region to the third_party faction.:::::disband_military_force;;;;;disband_military_forces: Disbands the targeted resource_mobile. Resource_mobile should be a military force.:::::faction_initiatives_clear_given;;;;;faction_initiatives: Clears the given initiative instead of setting it.:::::promise_of_perfection_take_unit;;;;;promise_of_perfection: Attempts to bribe the target unit to move over to our army in this battle. Only has an effect when used with cai_activation_point "z_prebattle_unit_bribery".:::::province_initiatives_clear;;;;;province_initiatives: Clears all selected provincial initiatives in the targeted faction_province.:::::region_initiatives_clear_given;;;;;region_initiatives: Clears all selected Region initiatives of the selected target. Supports initiative set or initiative set and initiative together.:::::rift_teleport_to_poi;;;;;rift_teleport: Teleports to the targeted point-of-interest.:::::trespass_warning_accept;;;;;trespass_warning: Accepts a trespass warning / "get-off-my-land" demand that has been given to us by the targeted faction. Targeted faction should have given us a warning. Intended (but not strictly required) to be used with cai_activation_point "z_received_trespass_warning". Generally has the effect of changing the AI allocator behavior and trespass analysis to attempt to withdraw from the targeted faction's regions.:::::winds_of_magic_decrease_strength;;;;;manipulate_winds_of_magic: Attempts to decrease the winds of magic strength in the targeted province.:::::winds_of_magic_increase_strength;;;;;manipulate_winds_of_magic: Attempts to increase the winds of magic strength in the targeted province.

add_points_of_interest_with_type;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "point_of_interest". Adds all PoIs of the type modifier_point_of_interest_type to the domain.:::::add_regions_with_region_hint;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "region". Adds all regions marked with the region hint modifier_region_hint for our faction to the domain.:::::add_teleportation_network;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "point_of_interest". Adds specific teleportation network.:::::grow_regions_from_seeds;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "region". Grows domain to include surrounding regions, dependent on modifier_region_range and modifier_allow_land_sea_transition:::::occupation_decision_captured_region;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "region" with activation point "z_occupation_decision". Adds the captured region to the domain.:::::occupation_decision_capturing_character;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "character" with activation point "z_occupation_decision". Adds the character that is capturing the region to the domain.:::::our_agents_with_plague_recipe;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "resource_mobile". Adds all of our agents that have a specified plague_recipe to the domain:::::our_faction;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "faction". Adds the current analyzing faction (i.e, "us") to the domain:::::prebattle_unit_bribery_enemy_armies;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "resource_mobile" with activation point "z_prebattle_unit_bribery". Adds all enemy armies facing us in the battle.:::::prebattle_unit_bribery_our_army;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "resource_mobile" with activation point "z_prebattle_unit_bribery". Adds our army that is potentially performing unit bribery.:::::rift_realm_using_character;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "region" with activation point "z_rift_realm". Adds the character that is using a rift to teleport to the domain.:::::rift_teleport_using_character;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "character" with activation point "z_rift_teleport". Adds the character that is using a rift to teleport to the domain.:::::trespass_warning_sender_faction;;;;;Must be used on domain with type "faction" with activation point "z_received_trespass_warning". Adds the faction that sent us the trespass warning.

modifier_allow_land_sea_transition;;;;;(bool) Used by grow_regions_from_seeds modifier to determine whether or not we can cross from land to sea regions:::::modifier_plague_recipe;;;;;(cai_plague_recipes key) Used by our_agents_with_plague_recipe modifier to add our agents using this recipe:::::modifier_point_of_interest_type;;;;;("GENERIC_MARKER", "WH3_RIFT_NETWORK") Used by add_points_of_interest_with_type modifier to add PoIs with the given type:::::modifier_region_hint;;;;;(cai_region_hints key) Used by add_regions_with_region_hint modifier to add all regions marked by this specific region hint:::::modifier_region_range;;;;;(cardinal) Used by grow_regions_from_seeds modifier to determine how many regions outwards to add. 0: this region, 1: this region and surrounding regions, etc.:::::modifier_teleportation_network;;;;;(teleportation_network key) Used by add_teleportation_networks modifier to add teleportation network POIs of a specific network:::::when_root_include_sea_regions;;;;;(bool) If we are a root domain, this determines whether or not we include sea regions.:::::when_root_include_unknown_items;;;;;(bool) If we are a root domain, this determines whether or not we include unknown items (items owned by factions we haven't met).

agent_subtype;;;;;(agent_subtypes key) Used by agent subtype checking queries to determine what type we are checking:::::allow_land_sea_transition;;;;;(bool) Used by searching queries to determine whether or not we can cross from land to sea regions in our search:::::compass_direction;;;;;(compass_directions key) Used by compass checking queries to determine what compass direction we are checking:::::decision_item;;;;;(cai_decision_items key) Used by history checking queries to define what decision item we are checking. If this is null, then it defaults to the current decision item being analyzed.:::::decision_profile;;;;;(cai_decision_profiles key) Used by history checking queries to define what decision profile we are checking. If this is null, then it defaults to the current decision profile performing analysis.:::::default_query_result;;;;;(real) The default value a query will return when in an invalid state (for example missing contextual information). Database table information in scoring (e.g query_invert_result, query_weight) will still be applied to this value. However, other query variables are ignored: for example, queries that utilize min_max_behaviour will return the default_query_result directly, instead of passing it through the min_max_behaviour.:::::faction_feature;;;;;(faction_features key) Used by queries to check if a faction has a given faction feature:::::force_stance;;;;;(campaign_stances key) Used by stance checking queries to determine what stance we are checking or filtering by:::::force_type;;;;;(military_force_types key) Used by military force type checking queries to determine what type we are checking or filtering by:::::history_specificity;;;;;("any", "target", "target_or_third_party", "target_and_third_party") Used to define the level of specificity for the decision_item history queries. "any" checks for a decision against any target/third_party, "target" looks for a decision against the same target, "target_or_third_party" looks for a decision where either the target or the third party were involved. "target_and_third_party" is a directional equivilant of target_or_third_party: target_or_third_party doesn't differentiate between the target/third_party while target_and_third_party does. The former is useful for non-directional questions ("did I force faction a and b to go to war?") while the latter is useful for more directional ones ("did I force faction a to raid faction b?"):::::ignore_abandoned_regions;;;;;(bool) Used by searching queries to determine whether or not to ignore abandoned regions:::::ignore_armed_citizenry;;;;;(bool) Used by searching queries to determine whether or not to ignore armed citizenry (i.e garrisons):::::ignore_rebels;;;;;(bool) Used by searching queries to determine whether or not to ignore rebel regions/forces:::::max;;;;;(real) Generic max; see min_max_behaviour:::::max_random_extension;;;;;(real) Used to add randomness in min/max: When the max variable is used, a random number between 0 and this value will be added onto the max.:::::min;;;;;(real) Generic min; see min_max_behaviour:::::min_max_behaviour;;;;;("bounds", "bounds_exclusive", "scaled", "none") If "bounds", then the check types will return 1 if the checked value is between min and max inclusive. This is useful for "has at least X money" or "has less then X public order" type checks. "bounds_exclusive" is the same, but checks exclusive instead of inclusive. If "scaled", then the check types will return 0 if the checked value is below min, 1 if the checked value is above max, and linearly interpolate in-between. If "none", then we return the underlying value of the query without modification.:::::min_random_extension;;;;;(real) Used to add randomness in min/max: When the min variable is used, a random number between 0 and this value will be added onto the min. Please ensure that min + min_random_extension is not greater than max!:::::owned_by;;;;;("self", "self_or_allied", "only_allied", "neutral", "enemy", "any") Used by searching queries to determine the owner of regions/military force in the query. This is relative to the domain; i.e, if domain is an enemy, then "owned_by: self" means the enemy owns that thing, not the analysing faction! This also only includes known factions; even "any" here will only check known factions.:::::personality_region_group_identifier;;;;;(cai_region_group_policy_junctions key) Used to identify a group of personality region groups via identifier key:::::plague_recipe;;;;;(cai_plague_recipes key) Used by plague-recipe checking queries to determine the plague-recipe we are checking:::::point_of_interest_type;;;;;("GENERIC_MARKER", "WH3_RIFT_NETWORK") Used by PoI queries to determine what type we are checking:::::pooled_resource;;;;;(pooled_resources key) Used by pooled resource checking queries to determine what pooled resource we are checking the value of.:::::queried_domain;;;;;("source, "target", "third_party", "most_specific") In many cases, an object may be making an decision regarding something other than itself. This variable allows defining whether we are checking something about the object making a decision (source), the object being acted upon (target), or a tertiary involved object that may be required for targeting (third_party). Most specific chooses third_party if it's set, otherwise target, and finally otherwise source.:::::queried_domain_2;;;;;("source, "target", "third_party", "most_specific") "x_to_x" queries do comparisons, and this domain acts as a secondary argument of the other thing to compare against.:::::region_group;;;;;(region_groups key) Used by region group checking queries to determine what campaign region group we are checking:::::region_hint;;;;;(cai_region_hints key) Used by region checking queries if the region is marked by a specific region hint:::::region_lost_recently_time_horizon;;;;;(cardinal) Used by faction_to_region_check_if_lost_region_recently query to determine how many rounds back we check. Note, this is as yet limited to a max of 10!:::::region_range;;;;;(cardinal) Used by searching queries to determine how many regions outwards to search. 0: this region, 1: this region and surrounding regions, etc.:::::settlement_type;;;;;(settlement_types key) Used by queries to check the type of settlement:::::shared_state;;;;;(string) Used by shared state checking queries to determine what shared state key value we are checking.:::::spawnable_force;;;;;(spawnable_forces key) Used by spawnable force checking queries to determine what spawnable force we are checking:::::subculture;;;;;(cultures_subcultures key) Used by queries that check what subculture a faction uses:::::teleportation_network;;;;;(teleportation_networks key) Used to differentiate between different rift network POIs:::::trespass_warning_round_horizon;;;;;(cardinal) Used by trespass warning query to determine how recently the warning was received
